h1: The 7 Best Black Office Credenzas With Drawers, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Black Credenzas With Drawers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 black office credenzas with drawers scored on top load, locks, drawer layout, power and width, from 43 to 63 inches wide.
summary: The ModernMate 63 inch lateral cabinet is the best black credenza with drawers for most offices, with a 300 pound top rating, full-extension drawers, a lock and built-in power. The ModernMate 60 inch three-drawer unit is the better pick for sliding-door storage, the 59 inch lit display model is the showpiece, and the DEVAISE five-drawer cabinet is the budget rolling option.
intro: Wide furniture fails in a predictable way: the buyer measures the wall, orders the biggest credenza that fits, and then discovers the drawers cannot open fully because a door frame, a chair or a radiator sits two inches too close. Width is the headline number on a credenza listing, but clearance is what decides whether you actually use the drawers.

So this ranking starts from what the cabinet does at its width. We reviewed seven black credenzas with drawers, from 43 to 63 inches wide, using the listed top rating, drawer type, lock, shelf adjustment, power and anti-tip hardware. A black finish hides dust poorly and fingerprints well, so we also note where a design shows wear, and we left off any entry whose listing did not support a clear comparison.

products.name: ModernMate 63" Lateral File Cabinet with Lock, 2-Drawer Home Office Storage
products.verdict: A 1.18 inch top rated for 300 pounds, full-extension drawers, a lock and outlets.
products.description:
The ModernMate 63 inch cabinet pairs a 1.18 inch thick top with a 300 pound top load rating, two full-extension drawers that take letter, legal and A4 files, a lockable bottom drawer and two AC plus two USB outlets. It falls in the $200 to $500 bracket.

It claims first place because the top rating is the clearest number in the whole group, and a credenza that can carry a printer, a monitor stand or a stack of boxes without sagging is the one that stays useful. Full extension on both drawers exposes the back of each file, and the lock covers sensitive paper. The two-drawer layout is the tradeoff: it stores less than the three- and five-drawer units below.

Buy it if the credenza doubles as a work surface or a printer station. Skip it if you want maximum drawer count, and plan clearance in front of the drawers before you pick a spot.
cons: Needs a lot of wall space
products.idealFor: Offices that use the top as a working surface.
products.skipIf: You need more than two drawers.

products.name: ModernMate 60" Lateral File Cabinet with 3 Drawers, Open Shelves
products.verdict: Three drawers plus a sliding-door cabinet, with hanging rails built into the bottom drawer.
products.description:
This 60 inch ModernMate has a 60.2 inch top, three drawers and a sliding-door cabinet. The bottom drawer has built-in hanging rails for A4 and letter files, and two anti-tip wall anchors come in the box.

It ranks second because the layout is the most balanced for storage: you get shallow drawers for supplies, a filing drawer and a door that conceals clutter. It loses to the 63 inch unit on the stated top rating, since this listing gives none, and the listing shows no lock or power. The anti-tip anchors are a real plus for a tall black cabinet that will hold paper.

Buy it if you want a quiet storage piece to anchor a wall. Skip it if you need power at the surface or a locking drawer.
pros: Built-in hanging rails in bottom drawer
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants balanced, hidden storage.

products.name: ModernMate 60" File Cabinet with Drawers & Door, Built-in Charging Station
products.verdict: Six open compartments, three drawers, a door cabinet and a desktop power strip with USB.
products.description:
Sixty inches wide, this ModernMate mixes a row of six open cubbies with three drawers, plus a closed cabinet whose shelf moves up or down. A strip of outlets and USB ports sits on the desktop.

It lands third because it trades rigidity of purpose for flexibility. Six open compartments suit books, boxes and decor, which makes it the best display-and-storage hybrid in the group, and the built-in power strip is useful at the surface. The tradeoff against the first two is that open compartments collect dust on a black finish and offer no concealment for paper.

Choose it if the cabinet will serve as a sideboard in a shared room. Skip it if you primarily file documents and want a lock or a stated load rating.
cons: No lock or load rating listed
products.idealFor: Shared rooms where storage doubles as display.

products.name: 59" Filing Cabinet with Lock Drawers fits Legal Size for Home Office
products.verdict: Two lockable legal-size drawers under acrylic display doors with LED lighting.
products.description:
At 59 inches, this credenza puts two locking drawers beneath a pair of clear acrylic doors that carry an LED light. The hanging rods can be set four different ways, and legal-size folders fit.

It ranks fourth because it is the most designed piece here: the lit doors show off books, awards or a collection, and the rod options make the filing drawers genuinely adjustable. The cost is practicality. Acrylic doors scratch and show fingerprints, and a lit display cabinet fits a reception area better than a utilitarian home office.

Buy it if you want a statement piece with real legal-size filing. Skip it if you want a plain, hardwearing workhorse, and keep an eye on the price, which sits in the $200 to $500 bracket.

products.name: 43" Wood File Cabinet with Power Outlet, 2 Drawers, 2 Open Storage Shelves
products.verdict: The narrowest cabinet here, with two file drawers, open shelves and a built-in outlet strip.
products.description:
At 43.3 inches wide, this wood cabinet is the compact choice. It has a pair of file drawers whose rails can be set for legal, letter or A4 sheets, two open shelves, a power outlet with two AC and two USB ports, and anti-tip hardware.

It is fifth because the space saving costs capacity: a narrow top limits what it can carry and fewer drawers mean less filing. For a small room, a corner or a wall between a window and a door, that is the right compromise. The $100 to $200 price also keeps it accessible.

Buy it if wall space is tight and you want an outlet at the top. Skip it if you want a work surface or a lockable drawer.
products.idealFor: Small rooms and tight wall spaces.
products.skipIf: You want a large work surface.

products.name: ModernMate 4 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Filing Cabinet for Home Office
products.verdict: Four drawers in two sizes, a lock, outlets and an adjustable interior shelf.
products.description:
The ModernMate four-drawer cabinet mixes two drawer sizes, locks, includes a built-in power outlet with two AC and two USB ports and has an adjustable interior shelf height.

It places sixth because the listing gives fewer details about the width, top rating and file sizes, which makes it hard to compare with the 63 inch model above. The mixed drawer sizes are the strength: a tall drawer takes files and a shallow one takes supplies, which suits a desk drawer replacement.

Buy it if you want the most drawers with a lock and power. Skip it if you need a verified load rating or a clearly stated width.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want many locking drawers.
products.skipIf: You need verified size and load numbers.

products.name: DEVAISE 5-Drawer Wood Drawer Cabinet, Office Storage Cabinet, Black
products.verdict: Five drawers and a door shelf on four wheels, two with brakes, rated for 100 pounds.
products.description:
The DEVAISE is a black wood cabinet with five drawers, a storage-shelf door, four wheels with brakes on the front pair and a 100 pound evenly distributed capacity.

It finishes last because the 100 pound rating is modest, and a rolling base is less stable than a fixed one with open drawers. The drawers suit supplies, craft items and small equipment better than hanging files, and the listing does not mention file rails. For the $100 to $200 price it is still an easy way to add a lot of drawer space.

Buy it if you want a movable supply cabinet. Skip it if you plan to file documents or put a heavy printer on top.
pros: Five drawers plus a door shelf
Front brakes lock it in place
products.idealFor: Movable storage for supplies and small gear.
products.skipIf: You need to hang legal files.

methodology.title: Top load and construction
methodology.description: Stated top ratings, top thickness and capacity figures carried the most weight, because a credenza only works as a surface if it can bear load.

methodology.title: Drawer layout and filing
methodology.description: We scored drawer count, full-extension runners, rail options and legal, letter and A4 support, plus how useful the layout is for storage.

methodology.title: Security and safety
methodology.description: Locks, anti-tip anchors and brakes earned points, since a wide black cabinet loaded with paper is both a security and a tipping concern.

methodology.title: Power and features
methodology.description: Built-in outlets, USB ports and lighting count when they are practical, and we marked down features that complicate cleaning or access.

methodology.title: Width and price fit
methodology.description: Widths from 43 to 63 inches suit different rooms, so we judged each model against its bracket and the space it demands.

whatMatters.detail: A rating in pounds tells you whether the top can carry a printer, a monitor stand or a pile of binders without bowing. Particleboard tops thinner than an inch tend to sag, and a stated thickness of 1.18 inches is a good sign. Look for a figure in the listing and treat missing figures as a warning.

Full-extension runners let a drawer open completely, while cheaper glides stop at three-quarters. That matters for deep lateral drawers, where the back of the file hides. Check the listing for the words full extension and for which drawers have it, usually the bottom one.

A drawer lock deters casual snooping and protects documents in a shared house or office. Most locks on furniture are light-duty, so treat them as privacy, not security. Look for a lock on the drawer you will fill with sensitive items and check whether it covers one drawer or all of them.

Listed width is the top; the drawers need room in front to open, and doors need space to slide. A 63 inch credenza on a 70 inch wall is fine, but one against a radiator or a door swing is not. Measure the wall, then add 20 to 24 inches of clear space in front.

Built-in outlets save a strip, but they tie the cabinet to one wall position. Anchoring protects against tipping, which is a real risk when two loaded drawers are open at once. Check for included anchors or anti-tip hardware, and plan the outlet and the wall stud together.

cards.label: Sliding doors
cards.text: Doors conceal clutter and keep dust off paper. The ModernMate 60 inch three-drawer cabinet is the model built around them, and it works well in a shared room.

cards.label: Open shelves

howToChoose.subheading: For a Printer and Supplies Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A top rating above 100 pounds, outlets near the top, and a shallow drawer for paper and cables. Keep the printer toward a vertical panel and avoid a tight cabinet door that traps heat.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The ModernMate 63 inch has a 300 pound top rating and outlets. The 43 inch wood cabinet has an outlet strip for smaller printers, and the 60 inch charging cabinet offers a desktop power strip.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The cabinet will carry heavy equipment or hold sensitive files, because the 63 inch ModernMate gives you a stated 300 pound top and a lock in the $200 to $500 bracket.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need extra drawers or a small wall unit, since the 43 inch wood cabinet and the DEVAISE give useful storage for $100 to $200.

faq.q: Do these black credenzas fit legal-size files?
faq.a: The 63 inch ModernMate and the 59 inch lit cabinet list legal support, and the 43 inch wood cabinet has adjustable rails for legal, letter and A4. The 60 inch three-drawer unit lists A4 and letter rails, so check each listing before you order.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with wide credenzas?
faq.a: Ignoring front clearance. Lateral drawers pull out about as deep as the cabinet itself, and doors need room to slide. Leave a couple of feet in front so you can open drawers fully without moving a chair.

faq.q: Is a 63 inch credenza worth it over a 43 inch one?
faq.a: Only if you need the surface or the storage. The wider unit adds a 300 pound top and full-extension drawers, but it demands a long wall. A compact cabinet suits smaller rooms better.

faq.q: How should I assemble a heavy credenza?
faq.a: Assemble it close to where it will sit, with a second person for the top. Fix the anti-tip hardware into a stud before loading the drawers, and check that the cabinet sits level.

faq.q: How do I keep a black finish looking clean?
faq.a: Dust with a microfiber cloth and wipe with a slightly damp one, then dry the surface. Avoid polish with silicone, which can leave streaks, and use coasters or a mat under lamps and printers.

faq.q: Can I mount a TV on top of a credenza?
faq.a: A TV stand on top is possible if the top rating allows it. The 63 inch ModernMate lists a 300 pound top, but other cabinets do not, so check the weight and keep the screen centered on the panels.

finalTake: Buy the ModernMate 63 inch lateral cabinet if you want a black credenza that can carry real weight and lock real files. Take the 60 inch three-drawer unit for storage that stays hidden, the 43 inch wood cabinet for a tight wall, and the 59 inch lit model when the piece needs to impress. The DEVAISE is the budget supply cabinet, and the rest are sound choices when their layout matches your needs.
